prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” HVAC company for Phoenix — the right choice depends on where you are, whether it’s an emergency, the type/age of your system, and your budget. I can point you to highly rated options, but first I recommend you tell me your ZIP code and whether this is residential or commercial and an emergency. If you want a quick start, here’s what to do and how to pick the best contractor for your situation.

If you want immediate help (emergency)
- Tell me your ZIP code and whether your house is safe to stay in. I can suggest 24/7 emergency providers near you.
- Meanwhile: check the thermostat batteries, change/inspect the filter, and check the AC breaker — sometimes it’s a simple fix.

How to choose a good Phoenix HVAC company
- Licensing: Ask for their Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license number and verify it online.
- Certification: Look for NATE-certified techs and EPA Section 608 certification (required to handle refrigerant).
- Insurance: Confirm they carry liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Reviews & complaints: Check Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/BBB for recent jobs and how they respond to complaints.
- Written estimate & warranty: Get a written diagnosis, itemized estimate, and a parts/labor warranty in writing.
- Upfront pricing & diagnostics: Ask about service call fees and whether estimates are free after diagnostics.
- Experience with your brand/model: If you have a specific make (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, etc.), ask if they service that brand.
- References: Ask for recent local references or photos of similar work.

Names commonly recommended in Phoenix (start here and vet with the checklist)
- Parker & Sons (large local company with HVAC, plumbing, electrical services)
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning / Benjamin Franklin franchises (24/7 service franchises often cover Phoenix)
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (national company with Arizona locations)
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (national, has HVAC branches in Phoenix)

Note: I listed common reputable names, but availability and quality vary by ZIP and crew. Always verify license/insurance and read recent local reviews.

If you want tailored recommendations
- Tell me your ZIP code, whether it’s residential or commercial, the AC make/model or symptoms (no cool air, short-cycling, leaking, noisy, frozen coil), and whether you need emergency same-day service. I’ll suggest 3–5 highly rated companies near you and what questions to ask them.
